newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity swaps managers at more than a dozen funds.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity swaps managers at more than a dozen funds.

text.p: Fidelity Investments Tuesday announced a shakeup of its mutual funds, naming managers to more than a dozen funds after two veteran money managers resigned unexpectedly last week.
The moves came after veteran fund managers Larry Greenberg and Andrew Offit both left to join other firms.

Greenberg had headed four funds: Fidelity Growth Company Fund, the Emerging Growth Fund, Fidelity Advisor Equity Growth Fund and Fidelity VIP Growth Fund, with combined assets of more than $21 billion.
He was considered one of Fidelity's top fund managers and was one of the few to head more than one of Fidelity's large diversified stock funds.
Fund watchers said Fidelity would have trouble finding a successor with as much experience. Fidelity ended up naming three managers to cover his four funds.

Steven Wymer, manager of the $2.1 billion Fidelity Dividend Growth Company Fund, was named manager of the $9.6 billion Fidelity Growth Company Fund, and John Hurley, manager of the $428 million Fidelity Select Software & Computer Services Fund, was named to head the $1.9 billion Fidelity Emerging Growth Fund, the nation's largest fund company said.

Jennifer Uhrig, manager of Fidelity Advisor Mid-Cap Stock Fund and the $1.7 billion Fidelity Mid-Cap Stock Fund, was named manager of the $6.2 billion Fidelity VIP Growth Fund and the $2.5 billion Fidelity Advisor Equity Growth Fund.
More than a dozen managers and research analysts were named to fill the posts being vacated by those who were promoted.

"We always keep talking about the strength of the bench and this is what you're going to see," said Teri Kilduff, a Fidelity spokeswoman. "This is the new generation of Fidelity managers that have been developed through the Fidelity system."
But since many other fund managers have left over the past year, some fund watchers said Fidelity's bench has been weakened.
"All of them are very young, have very little exposure to managing money," said one veteran Fidelity watcher who declined to be identified. "The experience levels continue to decline."
Many of the new fund managers have never managed more than a few hundred million dollars in assets, and are now being asked to manage billions, he said.

The shakeup was the biggest at Fidelity since early last year when the fund company switched the heads of 26 of its funds because of lagging returns. That was followed by the departure in May of Jeffrey Vinik, the embattled manager of Fidelity's huge Magellan fund.
Among the other changes announced Tuesday, Charles Mangum was named manager of Fidelity Dividend Growth Fund, succeeding Wymer. Mangum had managed Fidelity OTC Portfolio since June 1996.
Robert Bertelson was named portfolio manager of Fidelity OTC Portfolio, succeeding Mangum. Bertelson had managed Fidelity Convertible Securities Fund, also since June 1996.

Katherine Collins was named portfolio manager of Fidelity Mid-Cap Stock Fund and Fidelity Advisor Mid-Cap Fund, succeeding Uhrig. Collins previously managed Fidelity Select Consumer Industries Portfolio, Fidelity Advisor Consumer Industries Fund and Fidelity Select Leisure Portfolio.

A number of Fidelity's sector funds also changed hands, including the Fidelity Select Software and Computer Services Portfolio, Fidelity Select Leisure Portfolio, Fidelity Select Consumer Industries Portfolio and Fidelity Select Energy Portfolio.
